action: No action needed; for awareness. Japan Post business customers who received a notice should treat their sender contact details as seen by another customer.
date_note: Publication date of the disclosure; the company says it detected the problem and stopped the service on 8 October.
exec: A logic bug let one business customer see another's shipping sender data; a reminder to test access controls in customer portals.
plain: A bug on Japan Post's business customer site let some companies see other companies' sender names, addresses and contacts.
summary: Japan Post disclosed that a bug in the invoice ordering function of its corporate customer site JP Business Tool Box let one customer view sender information registered by others. Up to 4,807 records, with company and contact names, addresses, phone numbers and email addresses, may have been seen. The service was stopped on 8 October, affected customers were notified in writing, and most functions resumed on 27 October after a fix.
title: Japan Post: bug exposes other customers' sender details on JP Business Tool Box
